notable_absence.finding: Unlike backup-get-task-info.md, backup-manage-config.md, and backup-node-threads.md (this same batch), this page has no dedicated 'Required Permissions' heading at all - the Full Admin requirement is stated only once, in prose, inside the Curl Syntax section. backup-trigger-backup.md, backup-trigger-merge.md, and backup-trigger-prune.md (also this batch) follow the identical thinner pattern. The batch splits cleanly into two documentation templates: GET-oriented/informational endpoints get a structured, role-enumerated Required Permissions table; POST-action endpoints (pause/resume/backup/merge/prune) get a single Full-Admin-only sentence buried in the curl example. No page states this is deliberate.

cross_component_finding: Pause/resume is Backup-Service-only vocabulary: no cbbackupmgr CLI reference page in the corpus documents pausing or resuming a running backup operation (cbbackupmgr's own docs describe operations running to completion or being interrupted/retried, not held in a paused state). This is a genuine capability the Backup Service's scheduler adds on top of the shared repository/task substrate, not merely a different access surface for something cbbackupmgr already does - a data point on the 'separate thing' side of the round's central question, narrower in scope than the repository/plan/backup-data layer which this batch's other pages show is shared.
